title: Sebastian and the Bakery
premise: Lior Halloran ghostwrites celebrity chef Marguerite Voss's memoir while moonlighting as an anonymous pen-pal for a bakery's community outreach program, never expecting her assigned correspondent to be Sebastian Okafor, the baker whose lease Marguerite's restaurant empire is quietly squeezing out. Their letters deepen into love even as Lior, in person, becomes Sebastian's enemy—drafting the very memoir passages that paint his bakery as a failing relic. When Sebastian discovers both betrayals at once, Lior must choose between the career that rescued her from obscurity and the man who makes her visible; she exposes Marguerite's predatory lease scheme using the memoir's own drafts, forfeits the byline, and ends with flour on her hands, co-writing a small honest book about bread and second chances as the bakery's lease is renewed.
about_author: Ada Okonkwo is a former food-magazine editor who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming her own name. She lives above a corner bakery she refuses to name, on principle.

chapters.title: The Ghost Clause
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She signs the confidentiality agreement for Marguerite Voss's memoir, reminded of every byline she's surrendered. Introduces her rule: love stays in past tense. Emotional beat: competent loneliness disguised as ambition.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. His sister enrolls him in the bakery's anonymous pen-pal program to lift his spirits during the lease fight. He writes grudgingly about sourdough starters and stubbornness. Beat: guarded hope.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She takes the pen-pal gig for research texture, expecting a lonely retiree. Her first letter from 'S' is funny and prickly about developers. Beat: reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Flour Wars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In letters they spar over butter versus oil, tradition versus reinvention. In person, unbeknownst to either, their worlds brush: Marguerite's team scouts Sebastian's block. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Memoir Problem
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Marguerite dictates a chapter dismissing neighborhood bakeries as 'charming failures.' Lior writes it beautifully and hates herself. That night she lies to S about her work. Beat: complicity.

chapters.title: First Sight
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Lior visits the bakery researching 'a profile,' and he's disarmed by how she looks at bread like it matters. Neither knows the other is their pen-pal. Beat: unguarded warmth.

chapters.title: What the Letters Know
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She realizes she's telling S things she's told no one—including why she vanished from journalism after a retraction scandal. Beat: intimacy without a face.

chapters.title: Lease Terms
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The landlord offers renewal terms clearly engineered to fail; Marguerite's company has bought the building. He vents to his pen-pal, who goes quiet mid-correspondence. Beat: dread.

chapters.title: Two Names
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She connects the address in Sebastian's file to the memoir's real-estate chapter and understands she's been drafting his eviction. Beat: horror of complicity made specific.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A near-confession over cinnamon rolls; Lior almost tells him everything, instead warns him vaguely to get a lawyer. They argue about people who help from hiding. Beat: love brushing against duty.

chapters.title: Deadline Week
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The memoir excerpt leaks early—a gushing profile of Marguerite 'saving' the street—with Lior's distinctive phrasing. He recognizes her sentences like handwriting. Beat: recognition and betrayal.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts Lior with printed letters beside the leaked chapter; the same metaphors, the same hands. She doesn't deny it. Beat: climax of identity—the ghost seen fully.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone, she rereads every letter and drafts a resignation Marguerite will litigate over. Flashback to the retraction scandal: how invisibility once saved her. Beat: reckoning with fear.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lior sends the lease scheme evidence—an email trail she archived—to the tenants' association and a reporter, knowing it torches her career. Beat: justice outside the law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Marguerite Responds
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Marguerite retaliates publicly; Sebastian defends Lior at a packed community meeting, not because she's blameless but because she chose truth when it was expensive. Beat: love against duty, tested aloud.

chapters.title: Blacklisted
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Publishing doors close; her agent drops her. She applies to work the bakery counter, half-joking. Sebastian hires her, no conditions. Beat: humility met with grace.

chapters.title: Bread and Reparations
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Slow repair: 4 a.m. shifts, burnt loaves, conversations that don't flinch. Trust rebuilt through labor rather than apology alone. Beat: tenderness after rupture.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Court rules the renewal clause enforceable; the building's new owner honors it. The bakery survives—not saved by a white knight but by its own paper trail and neighbors. Beat: earned victory.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A small press offers her a book deal—for a story under her own name about ghostwriting and one stubborn bakery. She hesitates, then signs. Beat: reclaiming authorship of self.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First date that isn't a date: closing the shop, eating standing up, laughing. Lior says the thing about love being present tense now. Beat: quiet joy.

chapters.title: Proof Copy
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The advance copies arrive; Sebastian reads the dedication—his name, spelled out, hers beneath it. Marguerite's memoir flops honestly. Beat: vindication without cruelty.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Dual POV finale. Morning at the bakery: regulars, sunlight, the new book on the counter beside the register. Two people who chose each other over safety, flipping the sign to OPEN. Beat: home, finally, in full view.
